chunks.arabic_text: غَيْبَةِ الطُّوسِيّ: بِإِسْنَادِهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ

translations.en: Ghayba of al-Tusi: Via his chain to Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Umar who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام يَقُولُ فِي ابْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ: أَلَيْسَ هُوَ الَّذِي يُرْوَى أَنَّ… وَقَالَ: إِنَّ أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام يَعُودُ إِلَى ثَمَانِيَةِ أَشْهُرٍ! فَمَا اسْتَبَانَ لَهُمْ كَذِبَهُ؟!

translations.en: I heard al-Ridha (peace be upon him) saying about Ibn Abi Hamza: isn't he the one who narrates that … and he said: Aba Ibrahim (peace be upon him) will return within eight months! Has his lie not become apparent to you?!

en.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) uses the specific claim of Imam al-Kadhim’s return within eight months to expose Ibn Abi Hamza’s unreliability, illustrating how early Shia scholars scrutinized the accuracy of narrators' memories against established timelines. This critique underscores the rigorous methodology of hadith verification in Shia tradition, where even minor chronological discrepancies in eschatological reports were sufficient to question a narrator's credibility.
en.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about Ibn Abi Hamza's claim regarding the return of Imam al-Kadhim?

key_terms.ابْنُ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ: Ibn Abi Hamza, a companion known for narrating hadith
key_terms.أَبُو إِبْرِيم: Aba Ibrahim, a kunya for Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الغَيْبَة: Ghayba, the occultation or period of absence of the Imam
